children: The proposed issue includes a fresh issue of up to Rs 200 crore and an offer for sale of up to 5 crore shares

Iris Global Services, an information technology distribution and services company, has filed draft papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO).

The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 200 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 5 crore equity shares by promoter shareholders. The company plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to meet working capital requirements and for general corporate purposes.
Promoters Sanjiv Krishen and Kamini Talwar will partially offload their holdings through the OFS. The promoters currently hold more than 98 per cent of the company, according to the filing details.

Iris Global Services was established in 2009 and is based in New Delhi. The company operates in IT distribution and services, providing technology products and solutions across different areas of information technology.
The company is also considering a pre-IPO placement of up to Rs 40 crore. If completed, the size of the fresh issue will be reduced accordingly.
The IPO proceeds are expected to support Iris Global Services' working capital needs as the company strengthens operations and expands its business.
Pantomath Capital Advisors is the sole book-running lead manager for the proposed issue, while KFin Technologies has been appointed as the registrar.

The proposed listing comes as Indian companies across technology and services sectors continue to tap the primary market for growth capital. Iris Global Services' issue will comprise both fresh capital for the company and an OFS component for existing shareholders.
